strings.evidence.heading: What the satellites see at the farm
strings.evidence.veg.heading: Greenness through the year (NDVI)
strings.evidence.veg.what: NDVI is a number for how green the land looks from space. Near 0.1 means bare ground. 0.6 or more means thick green plants. It shows when the land near the farm is covered with plants and when it is bare.
strings.evidence.veg.low: Least green months (the land is most bare): {months}.
strings.evidence.veg.season: Season {season} ({months}): average NDVI {mean}, in a dry year {p20}, in a wet year {p80}.
strings.evidence.veg.check_ok: The greenest months fall inside our season windows and the land is least green in January to March, before planting. But the curve stays flat between the two seasons, so greenness alone cannot separate them.
strings.evidence.veg.check_off: The greenest months do not match our season windows. Check the windows with a local farmer or crop calendar.
strings.evidence.veg.limit: Each square of the satellite picture is about 6 ha. This farm is 2 ha. So the picture also includes the land around the farm. Trees or banana next to the field can hide the bare times. Clouds leave gaps. Only the farmer knows what is growing in the field.
strings.evidence.veg.source: Source: NASA MODIS, 250 m, every 16 days, {start} to {end}.
strings.evidence.terrain.heading: The lie of the land
strings.evidence.terrain.position: Where the farm sits on the land
strings.evidence.terrain.frost_none: No danger here: the coldest night in 25 years stayed above 14 °C.
strings.evidence.terrain.limit: The height map is made of 30 m squares. This 2 ha farm covers only a few squares. It shows the shape of the land, not small dips or ridges in your field.
strings.evidence.footprint: We assume the farm is a 140 m square centred on the farm point.
strings.evidence.pos.high: high ground: rain water flows away from the farm
strings.evidence.pos.low: low ground: rain water from higher land may gather here
strings.evidence.pos.mid: middle of a slope: not clearly high or low
strings.evidence.rain.heading: Three rainfall estimates compared
strings.evidence.rain.note: Three different ways of measuring the rain at the farm. NASA POWER and ERA5 are computer weather records, and they agree closely. GPM IMERG is measured from satellites and shows more rain. We do not know which one is right for this farm. A rain gauge (a cup that catches rain) would show it. So the app shows all three.
strings.evidence.rain.col.et0: Water the sun and wind can dry up (ET0)
strings.evidence.rain.et0_note: ET0 is how much water the sun and wind can dry up in one season from green grass that has all the water it needs. A crop uses a share of this amount. If ET0 is more than the rain, the crops depend on water stored in the soil.
strings.evidence.rain.source: Sources: NASA POWER, NASA GPM IMERG, ERA5 (ECMWF, via Open-Meteo; ET0 computed by Open-Meteo).
strings.evidence.field.heading: On the farm square itself (30 m)
strings.evidence.field.what: Landsat can see details of 30 m, so it can look at a 140 m square about the size of this farm. Green bars show how green that square is. Grey bars show the wider area seen by MODIS, for comparison.
strings.evidence.field.bare_heading: How often the farm square looks bare, by month
strings.evidence.field.bare_what: Share of clear satellite pictures in which the land looked bare (NDVI below 0.25).
strings.evidence.field.least: Least green months on the farm square: {months}.
strings.evidence.field.thin: Few clear pictures (fewer than 8) in: {months}. Use those months with care.
strings.evidence.field.season: Season {season}: average NDVI {mean}; bare in {bare} % of clear pictures.
strings.evidence.field.source: Source: NASA/USGS Landsat 8 and 9, 30 m, {clear} clear pictures, {start} to {end}.
strings.evidence.field.limit: The 140 m square is our guess, not a measured boundary. Clouds remove many pictures in the rainy months. NDVI cannot tell which crop is growing or why land is bare.
